## Implement seqconsistency Phase-1 MVP package

```
level: high
date: 2026-10-21
```

### description

Implement a complete, pip-installable Python package `seqconsistency` that assesses
whether multiple sequencing datasets (FASTQ SE/PE, coordinate-sorted BAM; profiles
paired_short / merged_short / ont / hifi) are structurally valid, technically
consistent, and poolable under an explicit policy, with deterministic bounded-memory
sampling, Wasserstein + Jensen–Shannon pairwise comparisons, five explicit-path
Parquet outputs, provenance JSON, optional HTML report, comprehensive tests,
benchmarks with measured results, and full documentation.

### result

1. Implemented the full Phase-1 package: FASTQ/BAM streaming engines, strict manifest and policy validation, deterministic reservoir sampling.
2. Implemented Wasserstein-1 and base-2 Jensen–Shannon comparisons, decision engine with stable reason codes, five versioned Parquet tables, provenance JSON, HTML report, CLI with explicit output paths.
3. Implemented scientific semantics: declared-vs-verified identity distinction, missing evidence never passes, thresholds shipped illustrative/uncalibrated, nontransitive pairwise handling.
4. Verified with 165 passing tests (structural, statistical, reproducibility across worker counts, policy, outputs, error paths, bounded memory); mypy strict and ruff clean.
5. Verified eight end-to-end examples producing intended decisions with correct exit codes.
6. Benchmarked with measured committed results (throughput, worker scaling, pair scaling, flat peak RSS at 4× reads) and documented bottlenecks before any native optimization.

### change

Files: created `src/seqconsistency/**` (17 files), `tests/**` (9 files),
`benchmarks/bench.py`, `benchmarks/render_results.py`,
`benchmarks/results-2026-10-21.{json,md}`, `examples/{make_examples.py,run_examples.sh}`,
`policies/example-illustrative.yaml`, `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`,
`docs/plans/**`, `docs/misc/**`; updated `pixi.toml`, `pixi.lock`, `.gitignore`.
Packages (pixi default env): numpy, scipy, pyarrow, pysam, pyyaml; dev: pytest,
ruff, mypy, duckdb, pandas, types-pyyaml, scipy-stubs; editable self-install of
seqconsistency. Environments: none beyond the project pixi default environment.
Git: branch `main`, conventional commits for core, tests/docs, and final results.

## Apply agreed external-review fixes

```
level: high
date: 2026-10-21
```

### description

Apply the agreed disposition of an external code review: uncalibrated thresholds must
not approve, output collisions must cover every consumed input, the Phred+64
heuristic tightened, BAM metrics selected by profile, SM/RG metadata reconciled,
the quadratic BAM reservoir fixed, CASAVA contradictions detected, policy validation
hardened, optional fastp evidence non-blocking, and two missed Phase-1 metrics
(clipping, joint length/quality) added.

### result

1. Implemented all eight full-agreement fixes and three adjusted-design fixes with regression tests for each reviewer counterexample.
2. Fixed the BAM reservoir (368 -> 61k records/s, 166x, measured) and re-ran the clean benchmark; corrected the previously wrong pysam attribution in the docs.
3. Verified the full suite green, mypy and ruff clean, and all eight examples regenerated with corrected outcomes.
4. Documented two review disagreements (Phase-2 sourmash/coverage; retained-fraction metric naming) with evidence.

### change

Files: updated 10 src modules, `policies/example-illustrative.yaml`, 7 test files,
`examples/make_examples.py`, `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`,
`benchmarks/results-2026-10-21.{json,md}` (re-measured),
`benchmarks/render_results.py`; created `docs/plans/20261021-165647_review-fixes.plan.qmd`
and `...20261021-170329_review-fixes.report.qmd` (html render untracked).

## Apply external review round 2 fixes

```
level: high
date: 2026-10-22
cross-repo: seqconsistency
```

### description

Implement the user-confirmed disposition of a second external review: four P1
correctness holes (pooled mate comparisons hiding swaps, order-dependent
reference checksums, approval without any assessed threshold, TLEN orientation
bias in insert sampling), two P2 engineering items (unbounded comparison
retention, per-pair input re-sorting in Wasserstein), abort() logging, and
documentation for the one rejected point (keep the Phred+64 heuristic).

### result

1. Implemented all six fixes with regression tests built from the reviewer's own reproductions (each was independently reproduced before fixing).
2. Fixed the example fixtures the new per-mate check exposed (first-in-pair-only BAMs) and restored all eight documented example outcomes.
3. Verified the full suite (181 passed incl. slow memory tests), mypy strict and ruff clean.
4. Re-measured benchmarks on an idle machine: pair scaling −32–65%, BAM +4.6%, FASTQ within noise, peak RSS flat at 4× reads.
5. Rejected point 2 with evidence: removal would silently misread genuine Phred+64 files; documented the exact rejection window and resolution instead.

### change

Files: updated 10 src modules, 5 test files, `examples/make_examples.py`,
`README.md`, `benchmarks/results-2026-10-21.{json,md}`; created
`docs/plans/20261021-174833_review2-fixes.plan.qmd` and

## Fix reference_mismatch review no-op

```
level: high
date: 2026-10-22
cross-repo: seqconsistency
```

### description

Fifth external review (corroborating a parallel-session audit): the policy
loader accepts `review | incompatible` for `metadata.reference_mismatch`, but
only the incompatible branch existed — under review, differing manifest
reference_id values silently kept otherwise passing groups COMPATIBLE.

### result

1. Reproduced first (review -> COMPATIBLE, zero findings), then fixed: the review branch warns (GROUP_DIFFERENT_REFERENCES) and sets metadata REVIEW, never downgrading an existing FAIL.
2. Added a two-branch regression test (review -> REVIEW+warning; incompatible -> INCOMPATIBLE, unchanged default); 188 non-slow tests green, mypy and ruff clean.

### change

Files: updated `src/seqconsistency/policy.py`, `tests/test_policy.py`,
`README.md` (policy comment), `docs/misc/*` (this entry, rolling sync).
Packages: none. Git: main, one fix commit.

## First real-data run: two geneus barcode FASTQs

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-26
```

### description

The user asked to run the tool as a test on two real geneus single-molecule
FASTQ files (barcode241, barcode242) from one run.

### result

1. Ran check with an ont-scoped uncalibrated test policy: decision REVIEW; GC JSD 0.232 exceeds the illustrative 0.03 threshold, read-length/quality/N distances PASS.
2. Diagnosed the exceed: both per-read GC distributions sit in two bins (0.56/0.58) with swapped weights (78/21 vs 55/44) — a mix-proportion shift, not different read types.
3. Noted the TSV manifest requires all 13 headers with empty optional columns (first attempt exited 2).

### change

Files: appended this audit entry (run inputs/outputs under /tmp/seqc-geneus-test,
outside the repo; source data read-only). Packages: none. Git: main, one docs
commit.

## Ten pairwise geneus comparisons BC-1..10 vs BC-15..24

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-26
```

### description

The user supplied ten barcode pairs (BC-1 vs BC-15 through BC-10 vs BC-24)
and asked to compare each pair.

### result

1. Ran one invocation with ten pool groups (4.5 s): all ten REVIEW; GC JSD exceeds in all pairs (0.072-0.892) and read_length W1 exceeds in eight (41.6-48.7 bp).
2. Identified the structure: two read-length families (~535 vs ~580 bp; cross-family pairs fail length) and GC mixtures over three classes (~0.54/0.56/0.58) with barcode-specific weights.
3. Closest pair 01/15 (same length family, same 78/22 GC mix, JSD 0.072); most distant 10/24 (GC classes nearly disjoint, JSD 0.892); quality distances stay 0.04-0.10 Phred everywhere.

### change

Files: appended this audit entry (outputs under /tmp/seqc-geneus-test3,
outside the repo; source data read-only). Packages: none. Git: main, one docs
commit.

## Corrected shifan dataset: 14 within-run pairs and the two-run comparison

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-26
```

### description

The user corrected the earlier data pointer: the pairs (BC-1 vs BC-15 ...
BC-10 vs BC-24, plus BC-1 vs BC-11..14) live in the shifan Run0001 directory
(BC-N = Group_0_BarcodeNN), and the follow-up ask compares Run0001 against
Run0002 barcode-by-barcode.

### result

1. Re-ran the 14 pairs on the correct Run0001 files (3.4 s): all REVIEW; pair BC-1/BC-15 passes every threshold, 8 pairs exceed length (19-64 bp), 13 exceed GC (0.043-0.377).
2. Ran all 24 same-barcode cross-run groups (4.8 s): 23/24 pass length (only bc12 at 10.8 vs 10.0), GC 0.014-0.043 straddles the 0.03 ceiling, quality passes everywhere.
3. Calibration signal: same-barcode cross-run distances (GC<=0.044, length<=10.8) sit far below cross-barcode distances (GC to 0.377, length to 64) — the 0.03/10.0 ceilings land on the between-run band.

### change

Files: appended this audit entry (outputs under /tmp/seqc-shifan-pairs and
/tmp/seqc-shifan-runs, outside the repo; source data read-only). Packages:
none. Git: main, one docs commit.
